title: Causal forests find insufficient evidence for pancreatic treatment subgroups
summary: In 130 pancreatic-cancer records, learned survival forests yielded overlapping patient-specific treatment-effect intervals across several priors. The cohort did not identify profiles with greater or smaller inferred radiotherapy benefit. This is model-dependent uncertainty, not evidence that treatment effects are identical.
ai_technology: Dirichlet-Tree Bayesian Causal Forest; Bayesian additive regression trees
organization: TU Dortmund University; Amsterdam UMC; Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

evidence.tested: Retrospective TCGA cohort: 130 patients,36 receiving radiotherapy; censored accelerated-failure-time modeling with3,027 covariates and prior-sensitivity comparisons.
evidence.unknown: Nonrandomized treatment requires untestable no-unmeasured-confounding assumptions. Small sample, censoring and prior sensitivity limit heterogeneity inference. No individual treatment recommendation or proven average benefit; cohort largely overlaps an earlier analysis.
evidence.ai_role: Learned tree partitions and outcome/treatment ensembles estimate conditional survival contrasts and their uncertainty.

source_review.scope: Primary v1 Methods3.1, application5.5 and full cohort/model/result appendixF.5; exact front/history/status.
